content.thinking:
This "Consensus" arm uses interactive slider estimates with corrective feedback on scientific consensus figures (99%, ~100%), plus nuance about disagreement on net-zero timing (66%) — a well-crafted, interactive, counter-attitudinal design. I'm recalling that consensus messaging meta-analyses typically shift perceived consensus substantially, move belief by roughly 1-2.5 points, and have smaller effects on policy support, with interactive correction formats similar to Vlasceanu's stronger-performing arms.

The "disagreement isn't weakness" framing also builds trust by signaling integrity, openness, and competence — nuance about scientific disagreement can actually boost credibility. I'd expect this to be one of the stronger arms for both belief_post and trust: trust_multidimensional around 2.2 given explicit discussion of evidence and openness to revision, trust_post around 1.5, distrust_post around -1.2, funding_perceptions around 0.8, policy_role_mean around 1.0, inst_trust_mean around 1.0. For belief_post, since the message directly corrects the core claim about human activity being the primary cause, I'd expect a stronger direct effect there.

Refining these estimates further, and setting concern_mean, policy_general, policy_specific_mean, behavior_mean, donation_ams, and newsletter_signup at similarly modest levels consistent with the other arms.

Mechanistically it is strong: active guessing plus immediate feedback typically outperforms dry expository text, the evidence is counter-attitudinal for skeptics, and the transparency framing plausibly boosts perceived integrity/openness as well as competence. Consensus meta-analyses show large shifts in perceived consensus but only ~1\ttimes2.5-point gains on belief in human causation and smaller policy effects, so I place belief_post around +2 (dampened somewhat by pre-treatment anchoring but boosted by the direct restatement of the same claim) and the fresh multidimensional trust battery slightly higher at ~+2.3. Distrust should fall modestly but less than trust rises (asymmetric, floor-ish effects). Mechanistically it is strong: active guessing plus immediate feedback typically outperforms dry expository text, the evidence is counter-attitudinal for skeptics, and the transparency framing plausibly boosts perceived integrity/openness as well as competence. Consensus meta-analyses show large shifts in perceived consensus but only ~1	times2.5-point gains on belief in human causation and smaller policy effects, so I place belief_post around +2 (dampened somewhat by pre-treatment anchoring but boosted by the direct restatement of the same claim) and the fresh multidimensional trust battery slightly higher at ~+2.3.
